scenes.name: Throbbing Gristle
scenes.book: Postpunk. Romper todo y empezar de nuevo
scenes.author: Simon Reynolds
scenes.desc: Nacidos del grupo de performance COUM Transmissions (Fluxus, accionistas vieneses, sexo y fluidos corporales en galerías), Genesis P-Orridge, Cosey Fanni Tutti, Peter «Sleazy» Christopherson y Chris Carter giran hacia la cultura pop para desafiar a un público más amplio. El escándalo de Prostitution en el ICA (1976) los convierte en enemigos públicos. «Antimúsica»: sin batería, instrumentos tocados como un niño, el «Gristle-izer» (un sampler primitivo), infrasonidos, improvisación en directo y una «línea de montaje sonora». Su sello Industrial Records y el lema «Music from the Death Factory» bautizan un género. The Second Annual Report, el electro pop torcido de «United» y «Hot on the Heels of Love», D.o.A., 20 Jazz Funk Greats y Heathen Earth; coqueteos con la imaginería nazi, la pedofilia y el supervivencialismo militar de Monte Cazazza («Subhuman», «Discipline»). La «misión terminó» en 1981; P-Orridge funda Psychic TV.

podcast.title: "The X Files" Movie Soundtrack Spoken Word
podcast.body: Chris Carter, the creator of "The X Files," contributed a strange spoken word piece to the soundtrack of "The X Files" movie. This hidden track, found at the very end of the album, discusses a syndicate's secret vaccine against "black oil," the breakdown of their code of honor, and threats from within and without, mentioning agents Mulder and Scully. "It's a spoken word piece by Sirius Creator Chris Carter, and it's just too weird not to play here."

xref.title: Cultural Impact and Name Origin
xref.body: Even non-musicians were captivated by The Pixies' influence; Chris Carter, the creator of The X-Files, named the lead character in his series Millennium, Frank Black, after the name Black Francis adopted after the Pixies disbanded. "Chris Carter, the creator of the X-Files, named the lead character in the series Millennium, Frank Black, because that was the name Black Francis assumed after the Pixies broke up."
